text:
Pearl Alternative/Adult Education School had 11 Hispanic students in 2024-25
Pearl Alternative/Adult Education School enrolled 11 Hispanic students in the 2024-25 school year, 21.4% fewer than the previous year, according to the Michigan Department of Education.
Data show Pearl Alternative/Adult Education School enrolled 35 students in the 2024-25 school year. Hispanic students made up 31.4% of that total, the second-largest ethnic group. White students were the largest group, accounting for 62.9% (22) of the student body.
The school is part of Fennville Public Schools District, whose central office is in Fennville.
Of the four schools in Fennville Public Schools District, Fennville Elementary School had the highest Hispanic enrollment in the 2024-25 school year.
Academic performance in Michigan remains below pre-pandemic levels. The 2024 NAEP results show the share of students reaching the basic benchmark in core subjects is about 10 percentage points lower than in 2019—except for fourth-grade math, which declined by just 2 points.
Achievement gaps between ethnic groups persist. On average, Hispanic students scored 15 points below white students, and Black students scored about 30 points lower than their white peers.

| 2021-22 | 39 | 20 | 51.3% |
| 2022-23 | 44 | 17 | 38.6% |
| 2023-24 | 43 | 14 | 32.6% |
